text:
Marie: heads-up — customers hitting fallback routes in eu-premium are seeing weird token-count spikes and tool-calls failing. can we review compatibility rules?
Ben: saw that, logs show tokenizer mismatch + tool-calling schema errors. short thread first: which models were involved?
Jia: root model was `redwood-llama-70b-v2` (bpe-v2) -> fallback to `rw-70b-quant` (legacy-bpe). tokenizer_id differs, so prefix splitting changed token counts.
Marie: that explains the spikes. but tool-calling parity also broke: fallback variant doesn't support the `tool_calling_v2` hooks. requests with structured outputs got 400s.
Ben: current router only checks architecture + context length. we need to include tokenizer_id and tool_calling capability in the compatibility matrix.
Kevin: agreed. proposed schema (simple): `compatibility = { tokenizer_id, max_context, tool_calling_level }`. when picking fallback require tokenizer_id match OR apply canonicalization + re-tokenize with token-trim policy.
Olga: re-tokenizing client input at router sounds expensive and risky for latency. prefer we encode model profiles with `tokenizer_equivalence_groups` to avoid expensive ops.
Jia: +1 to equivalence groups. also need telemetry for these events: which fields do we emit? current telemetry only logs fallback_model and latency.
Ben: suggest telemetry fields: `original_model`, `fallback_model`, `fallback_reason`, `tokenizer_id_original`, `tokenizer_id_fallback`, `tokens_trimmed`, `tool_calling_compat` (true/false), `route_tier`, `region`.
DevOps-Bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1123. Assigned to @Ben and @Jia.
Marie: UX note: Console rollout page should clearly show when a rollout triggered a fallback because of tokenizer/tool-calling mismatch. customers keep thinking it's an unrelated regression.
Olga: for rollout UX, maybe a per-rollout compatibility report that lists incompatible devices/regions and a small diff of model profiles.
Kevin: Implementation constraints: router logic lives in routing-service (Golang). adding fields will need an API bump for model catalog (model profiles). debating: extend model profile with new flat fields or add a compatibility object. which do we prefer?
Ben: flat fields are easier for query but will bloat catalog. compatibility object keeps things tidy. no nested JSON in our internal DB? we already store blobs for model metadata, so object is fine.
Jia: also need a deterministic fallback ordering that accounts for tier & region SLOs. pseudocode:
```
for candidate in candidates_sorted_by_cost_and_tier:
  if tokenizer_equivalent(original, candidate) and tool_calling_compatible(original, candidate):
    return candidate
  elseif allow_retokenize and candidate.max_context >= trimmed_length:
    return candidate (with telemetry flag RETOKENIZED)
```
Marie: TL;DR: add tokenizer_id + tool_calling_level to model profiles; implement equivalence groups; emit expanded telemetry; show compatibility in Console rollout UI.
Kevin: timeline? small spike fix -> 2-week sprint for router changes + model-catalog schema + telemetry. Console UX follow-up next sprint.
Olga: can we add a temporary mitigation: for premium customers in EU, prefer fallback variants that explicitly advertise `tokenizer_equivalent:true` in the catalog until we finish the router change.
Ben: done. pushed a catalog flag `tokenizer_equivalent:true` for the main fallbacks in EU. will monitor.
DevOps-Bot: Deploy successful: routing-service v1.42.1 -> eu-prod.
Jia: action items: Ben add telemetry fields + schema; Kevin add model-catalog compatibility object; Olga update rollout UI spec; Marie coordinate customer comms.
Marie: thanks. I'll draft a short note for CS and PMs explaining why token counts spiked and what customers can expect. :thumbsup:
